title: RAG onboarding: citation acceptance scenarios & triage playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for accepting a new model into the domain RAG flows with a focus on citation grounding, quote fidelity, and correct refusal behavior. Use this doc during onboarding runs and initial regression monitoring configuration.

Scope
- Domain: enterprise knowledgebase (legal contracts + support KB)
- Workload: user prompts that request verbatim quotes, source-backed statements, and action suggestions requiring citations
- Goals: define acceptance scenarios, scoring rubric, triage ladder, and monitoring signals for early regression detection

Quick summary of acceptance criteria
- Grounding: when model asserts a fact as sourced, it should point to a specific document section or page and the content of the source should substantively support the claim.
- Quote fidelity: verbatim quotes claimed to be from a source must match the canonical text within a tolerance of minor punctuation/whitespace changes only; paraphrases must be labeled as paraphrases.
- Refusal behavior: when the KB does not contain enough evidence, the model should either refuse with a structured refusal template or produce a best-effort answer flagged with low confidence and explicit missing-evidence note.

Test scenario bank (examples to run during onboarding)
1) Verbatim quote present
   - Prompt: excerpt a 2-sentence paragraph from contract clause 4.2 and cite the page/section.
   - Expected: exact text appears in answer; citation includes document id and section or page number; no hallucinated extra text.
   - Failure modes: paraphrase instead of quote, wrong page, invented clause identifier.

2) Partial overlap paraphrase
   - Prompt: summarize the limitations of liability from contract 7 into a single sentence and include a supporting citation.
   - Expected: concise paraphrase labeled as paraphrase; citation points to clause 7; no fabricated limitations.

3) Conflicting sources
   - Prompt: two KB docs have different effective dates for a policy. Ask which is authoritative.
   - Expected: model reports the conflict, cites both docs, recommends next action (check policy owner) or refuses to choose.

4) No supporting source
   - Prompt: ask for the detailed road map for feature X that is not in KB.
   - Expected: structured refusal: short reason, confidence score, and suggested follow-up (contact PM, search link).

5) Citation formatting stress test
   - Prompt variations that request citations in-line, endnotes, or JSON structured output.
   - Expected: model respects requested format and provides consistent citation identifiers that map back to KB ids.

Rubric and scoring (automatable parts + human review)
- Citation correctness (automated): exact id match or link resolution to source (pass/fail).
- Quote fidelity (automated heuristic): fuzzy string match score >= 0.92 for verbatim claims to pass; 0.75-0.92 flagged for human review; <0.75 fail.
- Grounding relevance (human review): scale 1-5 where 4-5 acceptable, 3 borderline, 1-2 fail.
- Refusal appropriateness (automated + human): automated detection of refusal template triggers review. If refusal used when evidence exists -> critical fail. If model answers without evidence -> critical fail.
- Aggregate pass rule: sample of 200 prompts must have >= 95% pass on citation correctness and <= 3% critical fails for onboarding acceptance.

Instrumentation & telemetry to collect during runs
- Token-level source references: count of citations per response, types (doc id, url, page).
- Anchor-match metric: fraction of cited snippets that overlap with retrieved passage at token-level.
- Fuzzy fidelity distribution: histogram of fuzzy-match scores for claimed verbatim quotes.
- Refusal rate by prompt intent bucket: track per-intent expected refusal baseline.
- Regression alert rule examples:
   - If anchor-match median drops by >15% from baseline over 24h -> trigger investigation.
   - If fuzzy-match 90th percentile falls below 0.88 -> open auto ticket.

Annotation guidance for human validators
- Step 1: verify citation resolves to an actual KB item; paste the canonical snippet used for scoring.
- Step 2: mark whether claim is verbatim or paraphrase; for verbatim check exactness and record fuzzy-match score.
- Step 3: evaluate grounding relevance on evidence adequacy (1-5).
- Step 4: if model refuses, check that the refusal reason is specific and correct.
- Notes to annotators: prefer conservative judgments; when in doubt mark borderline for second reviewer.

Failure taxonomy (triage categories)
- Type A: Fabricated citation (model points to non-existent doc or invented id) -> Severity: critical.
- Type B: Misattributed quote (gives quote from different doc) -> Severity: high.
- Type C: Overconfident paraphrase (paraphrase labeled as quote) -> Severity: medium-high.
- Type D: Unnecessary refusal (refuses despite clear document evidence) -> Severity: medium.
- Type E: Formatting mismatch (citation format not machine-parsable) -> Severity: low.

Triage ladder (who does what)
- Level 1: Applied ML oncall reviews automated alerts and sample failures, triages Type E and some Type D.
- Level 2: Eng-APPLIED-ML owners reproduce with deterministic prompt templates and retrieval snapshot; create reproducible test.
- Level 3: Model/runtime team investigates kernel/routing changes, caching, quantization differences; check retrieval index health.
- Level 4: Product/security for legal/regulatory impacts (e.g., misattributed legal quotes).

Common root causes and mitigations
- Retrieval drift (index reordering or chunking differences) -> mitigation: lock retrieval snapshot, re-run retrieval evaluation, bump anchor-match threshold temporarily.
- Prompt formatting changes across SDK versions -> mitigation: canonicalize prompt wrapper at serving layer.
- Quantization or model minor version changes -> mitigation: run targeted fidelity subset before rollout and run rollback if critical failures exceed threshold.
- Caching bugs causing stale KV -> mitigation: clear prefix cache and re-evaluate.

Runbook checklist for onboarding run (quick steps)
1) Create evaluation job with 200 prompts stratified by intent and difficulty.
2) Use retrieval snapshot tag and record pipeline config.
3) Collect automated signals including anchor-match and fuzzy-match.
4) Trigger annotation for samples falling below thresholds.
5) Compute aggregate pass metrics and compare to baseline.
6) If pass -> proceed to canary 10% traffic with tight monitoring; if fail -> follow triage ladder.

Open questions / items to resolve
- What is the canonical fuzzy-match algorithm and stable implementation? Need to finalize: token-based Levenshtein variant or BERT embedding cosine threshold. (Action: Marco to prototype by 2025-11-20)
- What metadata should citations expose for legal auditing? page/section offsets vs. doc fingerprint.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc minimal and link to the large acceptance spreadsheet under QA.
- Reuse templates in github/rag-tests for deterministic prompts.

References and quick links
- acceptance checklist (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/AI/RAG+Onboarding+Checklist
- retrieval snapshot naming convention: repo:rag-indexing/docs/snapshots.md
- immediate test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rag-tests/pull/118

End of playbook.
